discovery: The Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class of kinetic roughening and its experimental confirmation
motivation: In 1986 Kardar and Zhang, with Parisi, proposed the KPZ equation. It showed that growing interfaces in the presence of noise, such as burning fronts, bacterial colonies, deposited films and fluid fronts in disordered media, share universal scaling exponents that no equilibrium theory predicts. KPZ became the paradigm of non-equilibrium universality and links interface growth to directed polymers in random media, to Burgers turbulence and to random-matrix statistics. Takeuchi's liquid-crystal turbulence experiments (2010 onward) gave a precise quantitative test. They confirmed the exponents and also the predicted Tracy-Widom fluctuation distributions, which depend on geometry, and so turned an abstract theory into measured physics. Together these contributions changed how a whole class of disordered, driven systems is understood: through exact universal statistics that apply across materials and scales rather than through the details of any one model. Parisi was honoured in 2021 for other work, so I nominate his co-authors together with the decisive experimentalist.
